label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Tolu, me o 😂 I’m in Biology 100L now, and Medicine and Surgery was what I applied for. JAMB 2025, I scored 251 and got Biology at a federal uni here in Lagos. So when you said you checked your portal and started crying, I understood that one very well.

The day I saw mine, I locked myself inside my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. My mum was still telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for like two months after that. I had to beg her to stop because how many people would I be explaining to? 😭 So please, don’t feel somehow because you’re disappointed. You had already pictured yourself doing one thing, then the portal showed you something else. It hurts.

But let me give you the actual gist, especially about this transfer matter, because both “transfer is a myth” and “just read hard” are not the full story.

**Can you transfer? Yes, but please don’t accept Biology believing Medicine is waiting for you after 100L.**

What our level adviser told us is that, in my own school, you need at least **4.5 CGPA out of 5**, AND there has to be space in Medicine. That “and” is very important. It’s not just get 4.5 and pack your bag to MBBS.

She said last year, about six people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty. She thinks over 40 people applied. Those are the figures she gave us, not numbers I personally verified, but you can see why I’m saying it’s possible without being something you can bank on. And that was the whole faculty, not six people from Biology alone.

She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs in JAMB and post-UTME. So your 268 by itself doesn’t establish that you’re eligible for transfer. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME, and I don’t want to use my own school’s information to promise you something your school may not allow.

Before your acceptance deadline, please go to the department/faculty and ask for the exact rules for your own school. If they have them written down somewhere, ask to see them. Ask about the CGPA, both admission cut-offs, whether transfers into Medicine are currently allowed, how available spaces are decided, and when/how you apply. Also ask what happens if you meet the minimum requirements but there’s no space.

Don’t just ask “can I transfer?” and leave with one “yes.” Ask what that yes actually involves. And don’t trust forum people over the school, including me. I’m telling you my experience, not giving you an admission guarantee.

That’s why I don’t agree with Kingsley saying transfer is a myth. Our adviser told us people actually moved. But favour’s “just read hard” also makes it sound simpler than it is. Reading hard matters, obviously, but it won’t create a space where there isn’t one.

And let me expose myself small: **my first-semester CGPA is 4.31. Not 4.5.** I’m still trying. I wanted Medicine too, and I entered knowing I needed good grades. Wanting it badly doesn’t automatically produce the result. I’m not telling you this to scare you, just so you know I’m not speaking as somebody who has already transferred and is now saying “it’s easy, just focus.”

As for Biology itself, no, I don’t think it’s a bad course. I think I was so upset about not getting Medicine that at first I wasn’t really looking at Biology on its own.

Our 100L courses include BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. So don’t come thinking you’ve escaped Physics and Maths because the course is called Biology 😂 Those two are the ones dealing with people. You’ll need to take all the courses seriously, not only the ones you enjoy, especially if you’re chasing that CGPA.

There are practical expenses too. My lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual was extra. Your school’s prices may be different, but just letting you know that side exists.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and somehow I was fine. That was actually the day I realised I liked what we were doing. Not “let me force myself to like this because they’ve admitted me already.” I was genuinely interested.

I’m enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected too. That doesn’t mean you’ll feel exactly the same way, or that Biology and Medicine are interchangeable. They’re not. But Biology isn’t automatically a terrible course because it wasn’t your first choice. You can be disappointed about Medicine and still discover things you like here.

The question I’d want you to sit with is: **if the transfer doesn’t happen, would you be willing to continue Biology?** Not whether you’d be excited about it immediately, but whether it’s a course you could honestly see yourself studying. If your whole reason for accepting is “I’ll definitely leave after first year,” please pause and get the facts first.

Rewriting is not wrong either. I won’t tell you to accept just because other people want admission. You’re the one who will attend the classes and do the course.

But staying home isn’t as easy as “one year is nothing” makes it sound, and another attempt doesn’t guarantee Medicine. My secondary school classmate, Ifeoma, rejected Pharmacy to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. I’m not saying that to predict your own result or say she was wrong. It’s just a real example of why “rewrite and get Medicine next year” is also not a promise anybody can make for you. If you choose to rewrite, let it be something you’re prepared for, with a proper plan.

Also, ask yourself privately whether you want to study and practise Medicine, or whether a big part of it is wanting to be “Doctor” for your parents. I’m not accusing you o. With my mum still announcing Medicine in church, you can imagine why that question matters to me. Family expectations can be loud enough that it becomes hard to hear what you actually want.

You still have a little time before the fee deadline. Use it to get proper information from your school, then talk through the options with your dad. Neither “accept at all costs” nor “reject immediately” is fair advice without knowing those details.

Cry if you need to, but don’t conclude that your life has spoiled because of what showed on the portal. Whether you accept Biology or prepare to rewrite, this is not the end of the world. I couldn’t see much beyond my disappointment in that room in Surulere. Now I’m here, still trying, and enjoying parts of a course I cried over. You don’t have to have everything figured out today.
